name: Nephropathy Secondary to a Storage or Other Metabolic Disease

criteria.description: Confirmed diagnosis of an underlying storage or metabolic disease known to affect the kidneys
Evidence of renal impairment including proteinuria, hematuria, or reduced glomerular filtration rate
Renal biopsy showing characteristic storage material accumulation or metabolic deposits
Exclusion of primary renal diseases or other secondary causes of nephropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Confirmed metabolic or storage disease plus clinical or histopathological evidence of renal involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including nephrology, genetics, and pathology.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected via biopsy in Fabry disease and related disorders
searchTerms: storage material accumulation in renal tissue

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic vacuolization of renal tubular epithelial cells

pathognomonic.notes: Early marker of nephropathy secondary to metabolic disorders
searchTerms: protein loss in urine progressing over time

common.notes: Includes decreased glomerular filtration rate and azotemia

searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney problems
blood pressure increase due to kidney issues
body swelling due to kidney leak
low red blood cells from chronic illness
chronic disease causing low blood count
low energy due to kidney disease

occasional.symptomName: Neuropathic pain related to underlying metabolic disease
occasional.notes: Seen in Fabry disease and other storage disorders

occasional.symptomName: Hepatomegaly due to storage material accumulation
occasional.notes: May be present in some storage diseases
Observed in some lysosomal storage disorders
searchTerms: heart muscle disease from metabolism problem

occasional.symptomName: Proteinuria with nephrotic range in advanced disease

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to renal disease
searchTerms: pulmonary hypertension due to kidney disease

rare.notes: Occasionally reported in metabolic storage diseases
Secondary to chronic illness and metabolic dysfunction

laboratory: Abnormal metabolic biomarkers specific to underlying storage disease (e.g., elevated globotriaosylceramide in Fabry disease)
imaging: Cardiac MRI demonstrating hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in some metabolic diseases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes associated with storage diseases (e.g., GLA gene mutations in Fabry disease)
Molecular confirmation of metabolic enzyme deficiencies
other: Renal biopsy demonstrating characteristic storage material deposits
Electron microscopy revealing lamellar or zebra bodies in renal cells

distinguishingFeatures: Different histopathological patterns without storage material
Amyloid deposits on biopsy with Congo red staining

redFlags: Rapidly progressive renal failure in a patient with known metabolic disease
Nephrotic syndrome onset in childhood or adolescence with systemic signs
Unexplained proteinuria with multi-systemic involvement suggestive of storage disease
references: Orphanet: Nephropathy secondary to a storage or other metabolic disease (ORPHA:93593)
